blocking_finding.title: Default-enabled goal tools remain in the native registry
blocking_finding.issue: The 32-entry `_CODEX_NO_TOOLS_FEATURES` tuple does not disable `goals`. In pinned Codex rust-v0.164.0, `Feature::Goals` is stable and default-enabled (`codex-rs/features/src/lib.rs#L1957-L1961`). `codex exec` initializes `state_db` (`codex-rs/exec/src/lib.rs#L715`), and the in-process app-server extension setup installs the goal extension whenever that state DB exists, with tool enablement controlled by `Feature::Goals` (`codex-rs/app-server/src/extensions.rs#L87-L97`). The goal extension exposes its goal tools on ordinary threads, excluding only review subagents (`codex-rs/ext/goal/src/extension.rs#L105-L112`, tool contribution at `#L545-L595`).
blocking_finding.failure_scenario: For either authorized SOL selector, the runner launches ordinary `codex exec` in a fresh scratch home. The static model catalog suppresses model-defined patch/code-mode/multi-agent tools and the command suppresses the listed feature tools, but `goals` remains at its default true value. Because exec has a state DB, the extension contributes goal tools, so the request tool registry is non-empty despite the no-tools contract.
blocking_finding.why_existing_guards_do_not_catch_it: `apply_patch_tool_type=null`, `experimental_supported_tools=[]`, `tool_mode=direct`, and `multi_agent_version=null` affect model/core tool selection, not this independently installed extension. `agents.enabled=false`, plan/request-input false, empty MCP, disabled plugins/skills/web, and scratch HOME likewise do not disable `Feature::Goals`. Current regression constants mirror the same omission, so the command-shape tests pass without asserting `--disable goals`.
minimal_correction: Add the exact feature key `goals` to `_CODEX_NO_TOOLS_FEATURES`.
Add `goals` to the regression expected-disable set and assert that the constructed Codex command emits `--disable goals`.

The two derived model records are constrained to the four declared changes only: `apply_patch_tool_type=null`, empty `experimental_supported_tools`, `tool_mode=direct`, and `multi_agent_version=null`; IDs, default instructions, reasoning, and other metadata are exact-compared without this reviewer reading full default instruction bodies.

Direct tool mode plus null model agent override correctly falls back to configuration, where agents are disabled. Loaded `tools.experimental_request_user_input.enabled=false` and `tools.update_plan.enabled=false` are explicit even though the config API projection omits them.
Fresh HOME/CODEX_HOME/XDG/temp, project-doc bytes zero, memories/cloud skills false, web disabled, MCP empty, and plugin/app/skill/core feature disables close the reviewed non-goal paths.

Real transport uses a file-auth symlink rather than copying/parsing credentials; native auth refresh writes through that symlink to the original auth file. Fixture transport does not link auth. Missing-auth and catalog-tamper tests fail before dispatch.

`pyproject.toml:27-32` packages the catalog plus license/notice assets. Provenance names the official rust-v0.164.0 models-manager source and truthfully describes the original as a canonical two-record extraction, not a full byte-identical source snapshot.

The recorded `16-tool-catalog-green.xml:1` reports zero failures/errors across 329 JUnit cases/subtests, and `17-clean-native-metadata-v1.json:1` records credential-free config/catalog acceptance without a thread, turn, auth link, or generation. These artifacts do not prove the residual goal registry is empty.
